gm: Prologue

dm: Thus have I heard at one time:
gm: Thus did I hear at one time.

dm: The Blessed One was dwelling in Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s park, together with a great community of one thousand two hundred and fifty monks and a vast number of bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
gm: The Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī in the Jetavana, the park of Anāthapiṇḍada, together with a great saṅgha of one thousand two hundred and fifty monks, and very many bodhisattvas, great beings.

dm: Then, in the morning, the Blessed One put on his lower robe and Dharma robes, took up his alms bowl, and entered the great city of Śrāvastī for alms.
gm: Then the Blessed One, in the morning time, put on his lower garment and dharma-robe, took his alms bowl, and went to the great city of Śrāvastī for alms.

dm: Then, having entered the great city of Śrāvastī for alms, the Blessed One ate his meal and finished his duties regarding food.
gm: Then the Blessed One, having gone to the great city of Śrāvastī for alms, partook of his meal and completed the action of eating.

dm: Having finished his meal and ceased receiving alms, he set aside his alms bowl and Dharma robes, washed his feet, arranged his seat, sat down cross-legged, straightened his body, and remained with mindfulness established before him.
gm: Having forsaken later alms-food, he put away his alms bowl and dharma-robe, washed his feet, and sat down on the prepared seat, crossing his legs, keeping his body upright, and establishing mindfulness to the fore.

dm: Then, many monks went to where the Blessed One was, and having arrived,
gm: Then many monks went to where the Blessed One was, approached him, and

dm: they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated him three times, and sat down to one side.
gm: bowed their heads to the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated him three times, and sat down to one side.

dm: At that time, the Venerable Subhūti was also present and seated within that very assembly.
gm: Also at that time, the Venerable Subhūti had assembled in that very retinue and was sitting there.

gm: Venerable Subhūti's Question

dm: Then the Venerable Subhūti rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, and knelt with his right knee on the ground. Facing the direction of the Blessed One, he bowed with palms joined.
gm: Then the Venerable Subhūti rose from his seat, put his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, bowed with joined palms toward the Blessed One, and

dm: He addressed the Blessed One in this way:
gm: spoke these words to the Blessed One:

dm: "Blessed One, it is wonderful how the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha, has so greatly benefited the bodhisattva mahāsattvas with the supreme benefits, and how the Tathāgata has so greatly entrusted the bodhisattva mahāsattvas with the supreme entrustments. Blessed One, it is wonderful! Sugata, it is wonderful!"
gm: Blessed One, the supreme benefit with which the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened Buddha has benefited the bodhisattva great beings, and the supreme entrustment with which the Tathāgata has entrusted the bodhisattva great beings—it is wonderful, O Blessed One! It is wonderful, O Sugata!

dm: Blessed One, how should one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle abide?
gm: O Blessed One, how should one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle abide?

dm: How should one practice?
gm: How should they practice?

dm: How should one properly hold the mind?
gm: How should they thoroughly control their mind?

gm: The Bhagavat's Answer

dm: The Blessed One spoke these words to the venerable Subhūti:
gm: The Blessed One spoke these words to venerable Subhūti:

dm: Subhūti, excellent, excellent!
gm: Excellent, excellent, Subhūti!

dm: Subhūti, it is so; it is just so.
gm: So it is, Subhūti, so it is.

dm: The Tathāgata has benefited the bodhisattva mahāsattvas with the most sublime of benefits.
gm: The Tathāgata has benefited the bodhisattva great beings with the supreme benefit.

dm: The Tathāgata has entrusted the bodhisattva mahāsattvas with the most sublime of entrustments.
gm: The Tathāgata has entrusted the bodhisattva great beings with the supreme entrustment.

dm: Subhūti, therefore, listen well and take it to heart.
gm: Therefore, Subhūti, listen and bear it well in mind, and

dm: I shall explain to you how those who have truly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should dwell, how they should practice, and how they should properly hold their minds.
gm: I will explain to you how one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should abide, how they should practice, and how they should thoroughly control their mind.

dm: "So be it, Blessed One," he replied.
gm: Having replied, "So it is, Blessed One,"

dm: The venerable Subhūti listened as the Blessed One had instructed, and the Blessed One spoke these words to the venerable Subhūti.
gm: Venerable Subhūti listened to the Blessed One, and the Blessed One spoke these words to Venerable Subhūti:

gm: Generating Bodhicitta

bo: རབ་འབྱོར་འདི་ལ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་ཐེག་པ་ལ་ཡང་དག་པར་ཞུགས་པས། འདི་སྙམ་དུ་བདག་གིས་སེམས་ཅན་ཇི་ཙམ་སེམས་ཅན་དུ་བསྡུ་བས་བསྡུས་པ། སྒོ་ང་ལས་སྐྱེས་པའམ། མངལ་ལས་སྐྱེས་པའམ། དྲོད་གཤེར་ལས་སྐྱེས་པའམ། རྫུས་ཏེ་སྐྱེས་པའམ། གཟུགས་ཅན་ནམ། གཟུགས་ཅན་མ་ཡིན་པའམ། འདུ་ཤེས་ཅན་ནམ། འདུ་ཤེས་མེད་འདུ་ཤེས་མེད་མིན་ནམ། སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་ཁམས་ཇི་ཙམ་སེམས་ཅན་དུ་གདགས་པའི་བརྟགས་པ་དེ་དག་ཐམས་ཅད་ཕུང་པོ་ལྷག་མ་མེད་པའི་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པའི་དབྱིངས་སུ་ཡོངས་སུ་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདའོ། །
dm: Subhūti, those who have truly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think in this way: "As many sentient beings as are included in the category of sentient beings—whether born from eggs, born from wombs, born from warmth and moisture, or born miraculously; whether having form or without form; whether having perception or without perception, or neither with perception nor without perception—all those sentient beings I shall lead to complete nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa that leaves no remainder of the aggregates."
gm: Subhūti, here one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should form this thought: 'As many beings as are subsumed in the collection of beings—whether born from eggs, born from wombs, born from heat and moisture, or miraculously born; whether having form or formless; whether having perception, having no perception, or neither having nor lacking perception; however many are conceptually designated as the realm of beings—all these I shall lead to complete nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder of aggregates.'

dm: "Even though immeasurable sentient beings are thus led to complete nirvāṇa, one should generate the mind thinking that not even one sentient being has been led to complete nirvāṇa."
gm: One should generate the mind thinking: 'Even though immeasurable beings have thus been led to complete nirvāṇa, no being whatsoever has been led to complete nirvāṇa.'

dm: Why is that? Because if they were to hold such a perception, they would not be called a bodhisattva.
gm: Why is that? Because they would not be called a bodhisattva.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, if a bodhisattva engages in the perception of a sentient being, the perception of a life-force, or the perception of a person, they should not be called a bodhisattva.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, it is because if one holds the notion of a being, holds the notion of a living soul, or holds the notion of a person, they would not be called a bodhisattva.

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva should practice generosity without abiding in phenomena.
gm: Moreover, Subhūti, a bodhisattva should give gifts without abiding in objects.

dm: They should practice generosity without abiding in anything at all.
gm: Without abiding in anything whatsoever, they should give gifts.

dm: They should practice generosity without abiding in form.
gm: Without abiding in form, they should give gifts.

dm: Likewise, they should practice generosity without abiding in sound, smell, taste, tangible objects, or phenomena.
gm: Likewise, without abiding in sounds, smells, tastes, tactile objects, or mental phenomena, they should give gifts.

dm: Subhūti, in this way a bodhisattva should practice generosity without abiding in the perception of characteristics.
gm: Subhūti, a bodhisattva should give gifts in such a way that they do not abide even in the notion of a sign.

dm: Why is that?
gm: Why is that?

dm: The Method of Training in the Conduct of the Six Perfections
gm: Training in the Conduct of the Six Pāramitās

dm: Subhūti, the mass of merit of a bodhisattva who practices generosity without abiding is not easy to measure, Subhūti.
gm: Subhūti, it is because the heap of merit of a bodhisattva who gives gifts without abiding is not easy to measure, Subhūti.

dm: Subhūti, what do you think? Is it easy to measure the extent of space in the eastern direction?
gm: Subhūti, what do you think? Do you think it is easy to measure the space in the eastern direction?

dm: Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One, it is not."
gm: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, it is not so.

bo: བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ཀྱིས་བཀའ་སྩལ་པ། རབ་འབྱོར་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་ལྷོ་དང༌། ནུབ་དང༌། བྱང་དང༌། སྟེང་དང༌། འོག་གི་ཕྱོགས་དང༌། ཕྱོགས་མཚམས་དང༌། ཕྱོགས་བཅུའི་ནམ་མཁའི་ཚད་གཟུང་བར་སླའམ།
dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, is it easy to measure the extent of space in the south, the west, the north, the zenith, the nadir, the intermediate directions, and the ten directions?"
gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, likewise, is it easy to measure the space in the south, west, north, the directions above and below, the intermediate directions, and the ten directions?

dm: Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One, it is not."
gm: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, it is not so.

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, in the same way, it is not easy to measure the mass of merit of a bodhisattva who practices generosity without abiding in anything, Subhūti."
gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, likewise, it is because the heap of merit of a bodhisattva who gives gifts without abiding in anything whatsoever is not easy to measure, Subhūti.

dm: The Accomplishment of the Rūpakāya through Generosity and Other Practices
gm: Teaching That the Rūpakāya Is Accomplished Through Generosity and So Forth

dm: "Subhūti, what do you think? Do you think that the Tathāgata should be seen by means of his perfect marks?"
gm: Subhūti, what do you think? Do you think the Tathāgata should be seen by the perfection of his marks?

dm: Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One, it is not."
gm: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, it is not so.

dm: "The Tathāgata should not be seen by means of his perfect marks."
gm: The Tathāgata should not be seen by the perfection of his marks.

dm: Why is that? Because what the Tathāgata has spoken of as perfect marks are, in fact, not perfect marks.
gm: Why is that? Because what the Tathāgata has taught as the perfection of marks is itself no perfection of marks.

dm: When he had spoken thus, the Blessed One addressed the venerable Subhūti in this way:
gm: When he had said this, the Blessed One said this to the venerable Subhūti:

dm: "Subhūti, to whatever extent there are perfect marks, to that extent there is falsehood."
gm: Subhūti, as far as there is perfection of marks, so far is there falsehood.

dm: To the extent that there is no perfection of marks, to that extent there is no falsehood.
gm: As far as there is no perfection of marks, so far is there no falsehood;

dm: Thus, one should view the Tathāgata as being without marks and signs.
gm: therefore, the Tathāgata should be seen as marks and no-marks.

dm: When he had spoken thus, the venerable Subhūti addressed the Blessed One in this way:
gm: When he had said this, the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:

dm: Blessed One, in the final five-hundred-year period of the future, when the holy Dharma is about to completely perish, will there be any sentient beings who will arise to form a correct perception of such explanations of the words of a sutra as this?
gm: Blessed One, will there appear any sentient beings in the future time, in the last five hundred years, when the true Dharma is being destroyed, who will produce a true perception regarding the spoken words of a sūtra such as this?

dm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, do not speak like that. Do not say, "In the final five-hundred-year period of the future, when the holy Dharma is about to completely perish, will there be any sentient beings who will arise to form a correct perception of such explanations of the words of a sutra as this?"
gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, do not speak like this, saying: "Will there appear any sentient beings in the future time, in the last five hundred years, when the true Dharma is being destroyed, who will produce a true perception regarding the spoken words of a sūtra such as this?"

dm: Subhūti, in the final five-hundred-year period of the future, when the holy Dharma is about to completely perish, there will arise Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who are endowed with morality, endowed with qualities, and endowed with wisdom.
gm: Subhūti, in the future time, in the last five hundred years, when the true Dharma is being destroyed, there will appear bodhisattva great beings who possess ethical discipline, possess good qualities, and possess wisdom.

dm: Subhūti, those Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas have not rendered service to only one Buddha.
gm: Subhūti, those bodhisattva great beings will not have served a single Buddha;

dm: They have not planted roots of virtue under only one Buddha.
gm: nor will they have planted roots of virtue under a single Buddha.

dm: Subhūti, there will arise those Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who have rendered service to many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas and who have planted roots of virtue under many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas.
gm: Subhūti, there will appear those bodhisattva great beings who have served many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas and planted roots of virtue under many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas.

dm: Subhūti, those who will attain even a single moment of faith of mind regarding such explanations of the sūtra as this, the Tathāgata knows them.
gm: Subhūti, the Tathāgata knows those who will obtain even a single thought of faith regarding the teaching of a sūtra such as this.

dm: Subhūti, those are beheld by the Tathāgata.
gm: Subhūti, the Tathāgata sees them.

dm: Subhūti, all those sentient beings will generate and gather an immeasurable mass of merit.
gm: Subhūti, all those sentient beings will produce and completely gather an immeasurable aggregate of merit.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, it is because those bodhisattva mahāsattvas do not engage in the perception of a self,
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, it is because those bodhisattva great beings will not engage in the perception of a self,

dm: they do not engage in the perception of a sentient being, they do not engage in the perception of a life-force, and they do not engage in the perception of a person.
gm: will not have the perception of a sentient being, will not have the perception of a living soul, and will not engage in the perception of a person.

dm: Subhūti, those bodhisattva mahāsattvas also do not engage in the perception of phenomena, nor do they engage in the perception of the non-existence of phenomena.
gm: Subhūti, those bodhisattva great beings will also not engage in the perception of a dharma, nor will they engage in the perception of a non-dharma;

dm: They also do not engage in the perception of non-perception.
gm: and they will also not engage in non-perception.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, if those bodhisattva mahāsattvas were to engage in the perception of phenomena, that itself would become for them a grasping at a self,
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, it is because if those bodhisattva great beings engage in the perception of a dharma, they would by that very fact grasp at a self,

dm: and it would become a grasping at a sentient being, a grasping at a life-force, and a grasping at a person.
gm: grasp at a sentient being, grasp at a living soul, and grasp at a person.

dm: If one were to engage in the perception that phenomena are devoid of a self, that itself would become for them a grasping at a self,
gm: Even if they engage in the perception of a selfless dharma, they would by that very fact grasp at a self,

dm: and it would become a grasping at a sentient being, a grasping at a life-force, and a grasping at a person.
gm: grasp at a sentient being, grasp at a living soul, and grasp at a person.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, a bodhisattva should not grasp at phenomena as being erroneous, nor should they grasp at what is not a phenomenon.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, it is because a bodhisattva should not wrongly grasp at a dharma, nor should they grasp at a non-dharma.

dm: Therefore, keeping this in mind, the Tathāgata has said that those who understand this discourse on the Dharma as being like a raft should abandon even phenomena, let alone what are not phenomena.
gm: Therefore, with this in mind, the Tathāgata has spoken: 'Those who know this dharma discourse to be like a raft should abandon even dharmas, let alone non-dharmas.'

dm: Furthermore, the Blessed One spoke these words to the venerable Subhūti:
gm: Furthermore, the Blessed One spoke thus to the Venerable Subhūti:

dm: Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: Subhūti, what do you think of this?

dm: Do you think that there is any phenomenon whatsoever by which the Tathāgata has fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
gm: Do you think there is any dharma whatsoever to which the Tathāgata has manifestly and completely awakened as unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening?

dm: Do you think that there is any phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has taught?
gm: Do you think there is any dharma whatsoever that has been taught by the Tathāgata?

dm: When he had spoken those words, the venerable Subhūti addressed the Blessed One in this way:
gm: When he had spoken thus, the Venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:

dm: Blessed One, as I understand the meaning of what the Blessed One has said, there is no phenomenon whatsoever by which the Tathāgata has fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
gm: Blessed One, as I understand the meaning of what the Blessed One has spoken, there is no dharma whatsoever to which the Tathāgata has manifestly and completely awakened as unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening.

dm: There is no phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has taught.
gm: There is no dharma whatsoever that has been taught by the Tathāgata.

dm: Why is that? Because the phenomena that the Tathāgata has fully awakened to, or that he has taught, are not to be grasped and are not to be expressed.
gm: Why is that? Any dharma whatsoever to which the Tathāgata has manifestly and completely awakened, or that he has taught, cannot be grasped and cannot be expressed;

dm: That is because it is neither a phenomenon nor the absence of a phenomenon.
gm: because it is neither a dharma nor a non-dharma.

dm: Why is that? Because noble individuals are distinguished by the unconditioned.
gm: Why is that? Because noble beings are distinguished by the unconditioned.

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: The Blessed One spoke: Subhūti, what do you think of this?

dm: If some son or daughter of noble family were to fill this trichiliocosm world system with the seven kinds of precious substances and give them as a gift, would that son or daughter of noble family generate much merit on that basis?
gm: If some son of noble family or daughter of noble family were to fill this three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system with the seven precious substances and give it as a gift, do you think that son of noble family or daughter of noble family would generate a great mass of merit from that basis?

dm: Subhūti replied, "Blessed One, it would be much."
gm: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, it is much.

dm: "It would be much, Sugata."
gm: Sugata, it is much.

dm: That son or daughter of noble family would generate a great mass of merit on that basis.
gm: That son of noble family or daughter of noble family would generate a great mass of merit from that basis.

dm: Why is that? Because that mass of merit is not a mass.
gm: Why is that? Because that very mass of merit is not a mass;

dm: Therefore, the Tathāgata speaks of a "mass of merit, a mass of merit."
gm: therefore the Tathāgata spoke of 'a mass of merit, a mass of merit'.

dm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, if a son or daughter of noble family were to fill this trichiliocosm of great thousand-fold world systems with the seven types of precious substances and give them as a gift, and if another were to take up from this discourse on Dharma even just a four-line verse and explain it to others and correctly demonstrate it, they would generate a mass of merit from that basis that is far greater, incalculable, and immeasurable.
gm: The Blessed One spoke: Subhūti, compared to some son of noble family or daughter of noble family filling this three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system with the seven precious substances and giving it as a gift, whoever takes up even just a four-line verse from this discourse on dharma, teaches it to others, and perfectly explains it will generate a much greater mass of merit from that basis, countless and immeasurable.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, the unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and perfectly complete Buddhas arises from this.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, the unexcelled, perfectly complete awakening of the Tathāgatas, the Arhats, the perfectly complete Buddhas arises from this;

dm: Because the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are also born from this.
gm: because the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are also born from this.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, what are called "Buddha-qualities, Buddha-qualities" are spoken of by the Tathāgata as being devoid of those Buddha-qualities.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, as for what are called 'the dharmas of a Buddha, the dharmas of a Buddha', because the Tathāgata spoke of those dharmas of a Buddha as non-existent;

dm: Therefore, they are called "Buddha-qualities."
gm: therefore they are called 'the dharmas of a Buddha'.

dm: The Eight Types of Noble Beings
gm: The Eight Stages of Entering and Abiding

dm: Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: Subhūti, what do you think?

dm: Does a stream-enterer think, "I have attained the fruit of a stream-enterer"?
gm: Does a Stream-Enterer think, 'I have obtained the fruit of a Stream-Enterer'?

dm: Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One, it is not so."
gm: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, that is not so.

dm: Why is that? Blessed One, it is because he has not entered into anything at all.
gm: Why is that? Blessed One, because he has not entered into anything;

dm: Therefore, he is called a "stream-enterer."
gm: therefore he is called a Stream-Enterer.

bo: གཟུགས་ལ་ཡང་མ་ཞུགས། སྒྲ་ལ་ཡང་མ་ལགས། དྲི་ལ་ཡང་མ་ལགས། རོ་ལ་ཡང་མ་ལགས། རེག་བྱ་ལ་ཡང་མ་ལགས། ཆོས་རྣམས་ལ་ཡང་མ་ཞུགས་ཏེ།
dm: He has not entered into forms, nor has he entered into sounds, nor has he entered into odors, nor has he entered into tastes, nor has he entered into tangibles, nor has he entered into mental phenomena.
gm: He has not entered into forms, nor into sounds, nor into smells, nor into tastes, nor into tangible objects, nor into dharmas;

dm: Therefore, he is called a "stream-enterer."
gm: therefore he is called a Stream-Enterer.

dm: Why is that? Blessed One, if a stream-enterer were to think, "I have attained the fruit of a stream-enterer," that itself would be his grasping at a self.
gm: Why is that? Blessed One, if a Stream-Enterer were to think, 'I have obtained the fruit of a Stream-Enterer', that itself would be his grasping at a self.

dm: It would be grasping at a sentient being, grasping at a life force, and grasping at a person.
gm: It would be grasping at a living being, grasping at a life, and grasping at a person.

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, what do you think?

dm: Does a once-returner think, 'I have attained the fruit of a once-returner'?"
gm: Does a Once-Returner think, 'I have obtained the fruit of a Once-Returner'?

dm: Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One, it is not so."
gm: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, that is not so.

dm: Why is that? It is because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that has entered into the state of being a once-returner.
gm: Why is that? Because there is no dharma whatsoever that has entered into the state of a Once-Returner;

dm: Therefore, it is called a "once-returner."
gm: therefore he is called a Once-Returner.

dm: Blessed One, if a once-returner were to think, "I have attained the fruit of a once-returner," that itself would be his grasping at a self.
gm: Blessed One, if a Once-Returner were to think, 'I have obtained the fruit of a Once-Returner', that itself would be his grasping at a self.

dm: It would be grasping at a sentient being, grasping at a life-force, and grasping at a person.
gm: It would be grasping at a living being, grasping at a life, and grasping at a person.

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, what do you think?

dm: Does a non-returner think, 'I have attained the fruit of a non-returner'?"
gm: Does a Non-Returner think, 'I have obtained the fruit of a Non-Returner'?

dm: Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One, it is not."
gm: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, that is not so.

dm: Why is that? Because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that has entered into the state of a non-returner.
gm: Why is that? Because there is no dharma whatsoever that has entered into the state of a Non-Returner;

dm: Therefore, it is called a non-returner.
gm: therefore he is called a Non-Returner.

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, what do you think?

dm: Does an arhat think, 'I have attained the state of an arhat'?"
gm: Does an Arhat think, 'I have obtained Arhatship'?

dm: Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One, it is not."
gm: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, that is not so.

dm: Why is that? It is because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that can be called an arhat.
gm: Why is that? Because there is no dharma whatsoever that is called an Arhat.

dm: Blessed One, if an arhat were to think, 'I have attained the state of an arhat,' that itself would be his grasping at a self.
gm: Blessed One, if an Arhat were to think, 'I have obtained Arhatship,' that itself would be his grasping at a self,

dm: It would be grasping at a sentient being, grasping at a life force, and grasping at a person.
gm: grasping at a sentient being, grasping at a life, and grasping at a person.

dm: Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Complete Buddha has declared me to be the foremost of those who dwell in the state of being without defilement.
gm: Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly and fully awakened Buddha has declared me to be the foremost of those who dwell without afflictions.

dm: Blessed One, although I am an arhat who is free from desire, Blessed One, I do not think to myself that I am an arhat.
gm: Blessed One, although I am an Arhat free from desire, Blessed One, I do not think, 'I am an Arhat.'

dm: Blessed One, if I were to think that I had attained the state of an arhat, the Tathāgata would not have declared of me, "The son of good family, Subhūti, is the foremost of those who dwell in the state of being without defilement."
gm: Blessed One, if I were to think, 'I have obtained Arhatship,' the Tathāgata would not have declared of me, 'The son of noble family Subhūti is the foremost of those who dwell without afflictions;

dm: Because I do not abide in anything whatsoever, I do not declare myself to be one who dwells in the state of being without defilement.
gm: and because he dwells nowhere, he is called a dweller without afflictions.'

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, what do you think?

dm: Do you think that there is any dharma that the Tathāgata obtained from the Tathāgata, Arhat, Perfectly Complete Buddha Dīpaṃkara?"
gm: Do you think there is any Dharma that the Tathāgata received from the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly and fully awakened Buddha Dīpaṃkara?

dm: Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One, it is not."
gm: Subhūti said: Blessed One, that is not so.

dm: There is not any dharma whatsoever that the Tathāgata, Arhat, Perfectly Complete Buddha Dīpaṃkara obtained from the Tathāgata."
gm: There is absolutely no Dharma that the Tathāgata received from the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly and fully awakened Buddha Dīpaṃkara.

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, if any bodhisattva were to say, 'I shall accomplish the adornment of the buddha-fields,' he would be speaking untruthfully."
gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, if any bodhisattva were to say, 'I will accomplish the array of the fields,' they would be speaking falsely.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, the so-called "adornment of the buddha-fields" is spoken of by the Tathāgata as a non-adornment, because those adornments do not exist.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, as for what is called 'the array of the fields, the array of the fields,' it is because the Tathāgata has taught them as being no array;

dm: Therefore, it is called "adornment of the buddha-fields."
gm: therefore, they are called 'the array of the fields.'

dm: Subhūti, because of that, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should generate the mind in such a way that it does not abide.
gm: Therefore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva, a great being, should produce the mind without dwelling in this way;

dm: One should generate the mind without abiding in anything at all.
gm: they should produce the mind without dwelling on anything whatsoever.

dm: One should generate the mind without abiding in visible forms.
gm: they should produce the mind without dwelling on form.

dm: One should generate the mind without abiding in sounds, odors, tastes, tangible objects, or phenomena.
gm: they should produce the mind without dwelling on sounds, smells, tastes, tangible objects, and dharmas.

dm: Subhūti, it is like this: for example, if a person were to have a body such as this, that is to say, if it were to become as large as Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains, Subhūti, what do you think? Would that body be large?
gm: Subhūti, suppose, for example, a person were to have a body like this: that is, as large as Sumeru, the king of mountains. Subhūti, what do you think? Would you think that body is large?

dm: Subhūti replied, "Blessed One, that body would be large."
gm: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, that body would be large.

dm: "Sugata, that body would be large."
gm: Sugata, that body would be large.

dm: Why is that? Because the Tathāgata has taught that it is without any real entity.
gm: Why is that? Because the Tathāgata has taught it as being no entity;

dm: Therefore, it is called a large body.
gm: therefore, it is called a 'large body'.

dm: Because it is without any real entity, therefore it is called a body.
gm: Since it is no entity, therefore it is called a 'body'.

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, what do you think?

dm: If there were as many Ganges Rivers as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, would the grains of sand in all those rivers be numerous?"
gm: If there were just as many Gaṅgā rivers as there are grains of sand in the Gaṅgā river, would you think that the grains of sand in them would be many?

dm: Subhūti replied, "Blessed One, those Ganges Rivers themselves would be numerous, so what need is there to mention the grains of sand in them?"
gm: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, if those Gaṅgā rivers themselves would be many, what need to speak of their grains of sand?

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, you must have faith.
gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, you should be convinced.

dm: You must understand this.
gm: You should understand.

dm: If a man or a woman were to fill as many world systems as there are grains of sand in those Ganges Rivers with the seven types of precious jewels,
gm: If some man or woman were to completely fill as many world systems as there are grains of sand in those Gaṅgā rivers with the seven precious substances,

dm: and were to offer them as gifts to the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and perfectly complete Buddhas, Subhūti, what do you think? Would that man or woman generate much merit on that basis?
gm: and give them as a gift to the Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly and fully awakened Buddhas, Subhūti, what do you think? Would you think that man or woman would produce much merit from that basis?

dm: Subhūti replied, "Blessed One, it would be much."
gm: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, it would be much.

dm: "It would be much, Sugata."
gm: Sugata, it would be much.

dm: That man or woman would generate much merit on that basis.
gm: That man or woman would produce much merit from that basis.

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, if someone were to fill as many world systems as there are with the seven kinds of precious jewels and give them as a gift,
gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, if someone were to completely fill that many world systems with the seven precious substances,

dm: and were to offer them as gifts to the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and perfectly complete Buddhas, compared to that, if someone were to take up even a four-line stanza from this Dharma discourse, and were to correctly explain and correctly teach it to others, that person would generate much more merit on that basis—countless and measureless merit."
gm: compared to giving them as a gift to the Tathāgatas, Arhats, perfectly and fully awakened Buddhas, if someone were to take up even a four-line verse from this discourse on the Dharma, explain it fully and correctly to others, and teach it fully and correctly, they would produce infinitely and immeasurably much more merit from that basis.

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, any place where even a four-line stanza from this Dharma discourse is recited or taught becomes a shrine for the world including gods, humans, and asuras. It goes without saying that anyone who takes up, writes down, holds, preserves, reads, masters, and properly attends to this Dharma discourse will be endowed with supreme wonder.
gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if the place where even a four-line verse from this discourse on the Dharma is recited or taught becomes a stūpa for the world with its gods, humans, and asuras, what need to speak of whoever takes up this discourse on the Dharma, writes it, holds it, keeps it, reads it, masters it, and attends to it properly becoming endowed with the greatest wonder?

dm: In that place, the Teacher or someone like a venerable guru resides.
gm: In that place dwells the Teacher, or someone like a guru.

dm: When he had spoken those words, the venerable Subhūti addressed the Blessed One as follows:
gm: When this had been said, venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:

dm: Blessed One, what is the name of this Dharma discourse?
gm: Blessed One, what is the name of this discourse on the Dharma?

dm: How should it be remembered?
gm: How should it be held?

dm: When he had spoken thus, the Blessed One addressed the venerable Subhūti in this way:
gm: When this had been said, the Blessed One said this to venerable Subhūti:

dm: Subhūti, the name of this Dharma discourse is the Perfection of Wisdom;
gm: Subhūti, the name of this discourse on the Dharma is the Perfection of Wisdom, and

dm: hold it in this way.
gm: you should hold it thus.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, because that which the Tathāgata has spoken of as the Perfection of Wisdom is itself not a perfection.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, because the very perfection of wisdom that was taught by the Tathāgata is not a perfection.

dm: Therefore, it is called the Perfection of Wisdom.
gm: Therefore it is called the perfection of wisdom.

dm: Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: Subhūti, what do you think?

dm: Do you think that there is any Dharma whatsoever that has been spoken by the Tathāgata?
gm: Do you think there is any Dharma whatsoever that has been taught by the Tathāgata?

dm: Subhūti replied, “Blessed One, there is no Dharma whatsoever that has been spoken by the Tathāgata.”
gm: Subhūti said, "Bhagavān, there is no Dharma whatsoever that has been taught by the Tathāgata."

dm: The Blessed One said, “Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: The Bhagavān said, "Subhūti, what do you think?

dm: Do you think that the number of dust motes in the great trichiliocosm world system is many?”
gm: Do you think that the particles of earth that exist in the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system are many?"

dm: Subhūti replied, “Blessed One, those dust motes are many.”
gm: Subhūti said, "Bhagavān, those particles of earth are many.

dm: “They are many, Sugata.”
gm: Sugata, they are many.

dm: “Why is that? Blessed One, it is because the Tathāgata has taught that those dust motes are not dust motes.”
gm: Why is that? Bhagavān, because whatever is a particle of earth was taught by the Tathāgata as not a particle.

dm: Therefore, it is called "dust motes."
gm: Therefore it is called a particle of earth.

dm: Because the Tathāgata has taught that those world systems are not world systems.
gm: Because whatever those world systems are, they were taught by the Tathāgata as not systems.

dm: Therefore, they are called "world systems."
gm: Therefore it is called a world system.

dm: The Major Marks and Minor Signs
gm: The Major and Minor Marks

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: The Bhagavān said, "Subhūti, what do you think?

dm: Should the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened Buddha be perceived by means of those thirty-two marks of a great being?"
gm: Should the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the fully awakened Buddha be seen by those thirty-two marks of a great man?"

dm: Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One, it is not so."
gm: Subhūti said, "Bhagavān, that is not so.

dm: Why is that? Because those thirty-two marks of a great being that the Tathāgata has spoken of were spoken of by the Tathāgata as being without marks.
gm: Why is that? Because whatever thirty-two marks of a great man were taught by the Tathāgata, they were taught by the Tathāgata as not marks.

dm: Therefore, they are called the thirty-two marks of a great being.
gm: Therefore they are called the thirty-two marks of a great man."

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, if a man or a woman were to abandon as many bodies as there are grains of sand in the Ganges river, and if someone else were to take up even a four-line stanza from this discourse on Dharma and teach it to others, that person would generate far more merit, immeasurable and incalculable."
gm: The Bhagavān said, "Subhūti, if some man or woman were to give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā, and if someone were to retain from this discourse on Dharma even just a four-line verse and teach it properly to others, this one would generate on that basis far greater, incalculable, immeasurable merit."

dm: Then, through the power of the Dharma, the venerable Subhūti shed tears.
gm: Then venerable Subhūti shed tears by the force of the Dharma.

dm: Having wiped away his tears, he addressed the Blessed One in this way:
gm: Having wiped away his tears, he said this to the Bhagavān:

dm: "Blessed One, it is marvelous how this discourse on Dharma has been spoken by the Tathāgata. Sugata, it is marvelous!"
gm: Bhagavān, it is wonderful how this discourse on Dharma has been taught by the Tathāgata! Sugata, it is wonderful!

dm: Blessed One, ever since I attained the eye of wisdom, I have never before heard such a discourse on Dharma as this.
gm: Bhagavān, since wisdom arose in me, I have never before heard this discourse on Dharma.

dm: Why is that? Blessed One, those sentient beings who will generate a correct perception regarding this explanation of the sutra will be endowed with supreme marvels.
gm: Why is that? Bhagavān, those sentient beings who will generate a true perception regarding this sūtra being taught will be endowed with supreme wonder.

dm: Why is that? Blessed One, it is because that which is a correct perception is precisely a non-perception.
gm: Why is that? Because, Bhagavān, whatever is a true perception is itself no perception.

dm: Therefore, the Tathāgata has spoken of "correct perception."
gm: Therefore the Tathāgata has taught it as 'true perception'.

dm: Blessed One, that I contemplate and have faith in the explanation of this Dharma discourse is not a marvel to me.
gm: Bhagavān, it is not wonderful to me that I realize and believe in this discourse on Dharma being taught, but

dm: Blessed One, in the future, in the final times, in the last five hundred years, those sentient beings who take up, write down, memorize, retain, read, and fully master this Dharma discourse will be endowed with supreme marvels.
gm: Bhagavān, in the future time, in the final five hundred years, those sentient beings who take up, write, hold, keep, read, and completely master this discourse on Dharma will be endowed with supreme wonder.

dm: Furthermore, Blessed One, they will not engage in the perception of a self,
gm: Furthermore, Bhagavān, they will not engage in the perception of a self,

dm: nor will they engage in the perception of a sentient being, the perception of a life-force, or the perception of a person.
gm: they will not engage in the perception of a sentient being, the perception of a life, and the perception of a person.

dm: Why is that? Blessed One, because the perception of a self, the perception of a sentient being, the perception of a life-force, and the perception of a person are precisely that which is devoid of all perceptions.
gm: Why is that? Because, Bhagavān, whatever is the perception of a self, the perception of a sentient being, the perception of a life, and the perception of a person, that itself is free from all perceptions.

dm: Why is that? Because the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, are devoid of all perceptions.
gm: Why is that? Because the Buddhas, the Bhagavāns, are free from all perceptions.

dm: When he had spoken thus, the Blessed One addressed the venerable Subhūti in this way:
gm: When he had said this, the Bhagavān spoke these words to the venerable Subhūti:

dm: Subhūti, it is so. It is just so.
gm: Subhūti, so it is. So it is.

dm: Those sentient beings who, when this sūtra is being explained, are not terrified, not frightened, and do not become alarmed, will be endowed with supreme wonder.
gm: Those sentient beings who are not terrified, not frightened, and do not become completely terrified when this sūtra is being taught will be endowed with supreme wonder.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, this supreme perfection of wisdom has been spoken of by the Tathāgata.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, this supreme perfection was taught by the Tathāgata,

dm: For those supreme perfections that have been spoken of by the Tathāgata have also been spoken of by immeasurable and countless Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.
gm: because whatever supreme perfection was taught by the Tathāgata, that has also been taught by immeasurable, boundless Buddhas, Bhagavāns.

dm: Therefore, it is called the supreme perfection.
gm: Therefore, it is called the supreme perfection.

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, that which the Tathāgata calls the perfection of patience is not a perfection.
gm: Moreover, Subhūti, whatever perfection of patience was taught by the Tathāgata, that itself is no perfection.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, at the time when the King of Kaliṅga severed my limbs and minor limbs, I had no notion of a self, no notion of a sentient being, no notion of a life-force, and no notion of a person.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, at the time when the king of Kaliṅga cut off my major and minor limbs, at that time the perception of a self, the perception of a sentient being, the perception of a life force, or the perception of a person did not arise in me, and

dm: I had no notion of anything, yet it is not the case that I became without notion.
gm: because I had no perception whatsoever, nor was I without perception.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, if at that time a notion of a self had arisen in me, then a notion of malice would also have arisen.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, if at that time the perception of a self had arisen in me, then at that time the perception of malice would also have arisen, and

dm: And if a notion of a sentient being, a notion of a life-force, or a notion of a person had arisen, then a notion of malice would also have arisen.
gm: because if the perception of a sentient being, the perception of a life force, or the perception of a person had arisen, then at that time the perception of malice would also have arisen.

dm: Subhūti, I recall that in a past age, when I was a sage called "Speaker of Patience" for five hundred lifetimes, even at that time I had no notion of a self.
gm: Subhūti, I remember that in the past, for five hundred lifetimes, when I was the sage called Kṣāntivādin, even at that time the perception of a self did not arise in me.

dm: I had no notion of a sentient being, no notion of a life-force, and no notion of a person.
gm: The perception of a sentient being, the perception of a life force, or the perception of a person did not arise.

dm: Subhūti, therefore, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should completely abandon all notions, and...
gm: Therefore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva great being should completely abandon all perceptions and

dm: One should generate the mind for unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment.
gm: give rise to the mind for unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment.

dm: One should generate the mind without abiding in form.
gm: They should give rise to the mind without abiding in form.

dm: One should generate the mind without abiding in sound, smell, taste, or tangible objects.
gm: They should give rise to the mind without abiding in sound, smell, taste, or tactile objects.

dm: One should generate the mind without abiding in phenomena.
gm: They should give rise to the mind without abiding in phenomena.

dm: One should generate the mind without abiding in the non-existence of phenomena.
gm: They should give rise to the mind without abiding in non-phenomena.

dm: One should generate the mind without abiding in anything at all.
gm: They should give rise to the mind without abiding in anything whatsoever.

dm: Why is that? Because whatever abides is itself non-abiding.
gm: Why is that? Because whatever is an abiding is itself a non-abiding.

dm: Therefore, the Tathāgata has said: "A bodhisattva should practice generosity without abiding in anything at all."
gm: Therefore, the Tathāgata has spoken thus: "A bodhisattva should give gifts without abiding in anything whatsoever."

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva should completely relinquish generosity for the sake of the benefit of all sentient beings.
gm: Moreover, Subhūti, a bodhisattva should give gifts in this way for the benefit of all sentient beings.

dm: Whatever is perceived as a sentient being is itself devoid of perception.
gm: Whatever is the perception of a sentient being is itself a non-perception.

dm: Those sentient beings that the Tathāgata has spoken of as "all sentient beings" are also non-existent.
gm: Those very sentient beings spoken of by the Tathāgata as "all sentient beings" do not exist.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, the Tathāgata is one who speaks what is authentic, speaks what is true, and speaks in accordance with suchness.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, the Tathāgata speaks authentically, speaks truthfully, and speaks of suchness;

dm: This is because the Tathāgata does not speak falsely.
gm: because the Tathāgata does not speak falsely.

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, there is neither truth nor falsehood in the phenomena that the Tathāgata has perfectly awakened to or taught.
gm: Moreover, Subhūti, in whatever phenomena the Tathāgata has fully awakened to or taught, there is neither truth nor falsehood.

dm: Subhūti, it is like this: for example, just as a person with sight who enters the darkness sees nothing at all, so should one view a bodhisattva who practices generosity while having fallen into the perception of entities.
gm: Subhūti, it is like this: just as a person with eyes who enters into darkness sees nothing at all, in the same way should a bodhisattva be seen who has fallen into objects when giving gifts.

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, it is like this: for example, when dawn breaks and the sun rises, a person with sight sees all various kinds of forms; in the same way, one should view a bodhisattva who practices generosity without having fallen into the perception of entities.
gm: Moreover, Subhūti, it is like this: just as when dawn breaks and the sun rises, a person with eyes sees various forms, in the same way should a bodhisattva be seen who has not fallen into objects when giving gifts.

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, any sons or daughters of noble family who take up this Dharma discourse, hold it, keep it, read it, master it, and extensively and correctly teach it to others are known by the Tathāgata, and are seen by the Tathāgata;
gm: Moreover, Subhūti, whatever sons of noble family or daughters of noble family take up, hold, keep, read, completely comprehend, and vastly and authentically teach to others this dharma discourse, they are known by the Tathāgata, seen by the Tathāgata, and

dm: all those sentient beings will generate an immeasurable mass of merit.
gm: all those sentient beings will produce an immeasurable heap of merit.

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if any man or woman were to sacrifice their body as many times as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River during the morning, and likewise sacrifice their body as many times as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River during the midday, and again sacrifice their body as many times as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River during the evening, and in this way were to sacrifice their body for many hundreds of thousands of millions of eons;
gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if a man or woman were to give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā in the morning, and were to give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā at midday and in the afternoon, compared to giving away bodies in this manner for many tens of millions, hundreds of millions, and hundreds of thousands of eons,

dm: if, having heard this Dharma discourse, someone were not to reject it, they would generate a mass of merit that is far greater, immeasurable, and countless; what need is there to mention one who writes it down, takes it up, holds it, reads it, masters it, and extensively and correctly teaches it to others?
gm: if someone, having heard this dharma discourse, does not abandon it, they would on that basis produce a much greater, incalculable, and immeasurable amount of merit; so what need is there to mention someone who, having written it in letters, takes it up, holds it, keeps it, reads it, completely comprehends it, and vastly and authentically teaches it to others?

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, this Dharma discourse is inconceivable and incomparable.
gm: Moreover, Subhūti, this dharma discourse is inconceivable and incomparable;

dm: One should know that the ripening of this is also inconceivable.
gm: its ripening should also be known as inconceivable.

dm: The Tathāgata has spoken this Dharma discourse for the sake of those sentient beings who have correctly entered the supreme vehicle, and for the sake of those sentient beings who have correctly entered the unsurpassed vehicle.
gm: The Tathāgata has spoken this dharma discourse for the sake of sentient beings who have authentically entered into the supreme vehicle, and for the sake of sentient beings who have authentically entered into the foremost vehicle.

bo: གང་དག་ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྣམ་གྲངས་འདི་ལེན་པ་དང༌། འཛིན་པ་དང༌། འཆང་བ་དང༌། ཀློག་པ་དང༌། ཀུན་ཆུབ་པར་བྱེད་པ་དང༌། གཞན་དག་ལ་རྒྱ་ཆེར་ཡང་དག་པར་རབ་ཏུ་སྟོན་པ་དེ་དག་ནི་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པས་མཁྱེན། དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པས་གཟིགས་ཏེ།
dm: The Tathāgata knows and the Tathāgata sees those who take up, hold, preserve, read, master, and extensively and correctly teach this Dharma discourse to others.
gm: Those who take up, hold, keep, read, completely comprehend, and vastly and authentically teach this dharma discourse to others are known by the Tathāgata and seen by the Tathāgata,

dm: All those sentient beings will come to possess an immeasurable mass of merit.
gm: and all those sentient beings will be endowed with an immeasurable heap of merit;

dm: They will come to possess a mass of merit that is inconceivable, incomparable, immeasurable, and limitless.
gm: they will be endowed with an inconceivable, incomparable, measureless, and limitless heap of merit,

dm: All those sentient beings will have my awakening placed upon their shoulders.
gm: and all those sentient beings will carry my awakening upon their shoulders.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, those who are intent upon the inferior cannot listen to this discourse on the Dharma,
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, those who are inclined toward the inferior are unable to hear this dharma discourse;

dm: nor can those who hold the view of a self, those who hold the view of a sentient being, those who hold the view of a life-force,
gm: nor by those who hold a view of a self, nor by those who hold a view of a sentient being, nor by those who hold a view of a living being;

dm: or those who hold the view of a person listen to it, take it up, grasp it, read it, or master it.
gm: and those who hold a view of a person are unable to hear, take up, hold, read, or completely comprehend it,

dm: That is because it is without a place of abiding.
gm: because that is impossible.

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, any place where this sūtra is taught will be worthy of being venerated by the world, including its gods, humans, and asuras.
gm: Moreover, Subhūti, in whatever place this sūtra is taught, that place will become worthy of being venerated by the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

dm: That place will be worthy of being prostrated to and worthy of being circumambulated.
gm: That place will become worthy of being bowed to and worthy of being circumambulated;

dm: That place will become like a reliquary.
gm: that place will become like a stūpa.

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, any sons or daughters of noble family who take up, uphold, bear, read, and master these words of such a sūtra will be tormented,
gm: Moreover, Subhūti, whichever sons of noble family or daughters of noble family take up, hold, keep, read, and completely comprehend these words of a sūtra such as this, they will be tormented;

dm: they will be severely tormented.
gm: they will be severely tormented.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, those sentient beings who, in previous lives, committed non-virtuous actions that would have led to rebirth in the lower realms, will, by being tormented in this very life, have those non-virtuous actions of previous lives that would have led to rebirth in the lower realms purified;
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, because they are tormented in this very life for whatever nonvirtuous actions those sentient beings committed in past lives that would lead to rebirth in the lower realms, the nonvirtuous actions they committed in past lives that would lead to rebirth in the lower realms will be purified,

dm: and they will also attain the enlightenment of a Buddha.
gm: and they will also attain the awakening of a buddha.

dm: Subhūti, I recall that in the past, even more incalculable than incalculable eons ago, before the time of the Tathāgata, Arhat, perfectly complete Buddha Dīpaṃkara, I served eighty-four hundred thousand million Buddhas and pleased them.
gm: Subhūti, I remember that in the past, in measureless and even more than measureless eons, before and even further before the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly and fully awakened Buddha Dīpaṃkara, eighty-four hundred thousand million myriad buddhas appeared, whom I pleased,

dm: Having pleased them, I did not displease them, nor did I cause their hearts to be troubled.
gm: did not displease, and did not disappoint.

bo: རབ་འབྱོར་སངས་རྒྱས་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་དེ་དག་ངས་མཉེས་པར་བྱས་ནས་ཐུགས་འབྱུང་བར་མ་བྱས་པ་གང་ཡིན་པ་དང༌། ཕྱི་མའི་དུས་ལྔ་བརྒྱའི་ཐ་མར་གྱུར་པ་ན། མདོ་སྡེ་འདི་ལེན་པ་དང༌། འདྲི་བ་དང༌། འཛིན་པ་དང་འཆང་བ་དང༌། ཀློག་པ་དང༌། ཀུན་ཆུབ་པར་བྱེད་པ་གང་ཡིན་པ་ལས། རབ་འབྱོར་བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་འདི་ལ་བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་སྔ་མས་བརྒྱའི་ཆར་ཡང་ཉེ་བར་མི་འགྲོ།
dm: Subhūti, regarding the fact that I pleased those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and did not cause their hearts to be troubled, and regarding the fact that in the final period, in the last five hundred years, there will be those who take up, inquire into, uphold, recite, read, and fully comprehend this sūtra—Subhūti, compared to this mass of merit, that previous mass of merit does not approach even a hundredth part.
gm: Subhūti, whatever pleasing and not disappointing of those buddhas, the Blessed Ones, I did, compared to whoever, when the last five hundred years of the latter time have come, takes up, writes, holds, keeps, reads, and completely comprehends this sūtra—Subhūti, the former heap of merit does not approach even a hundredth part of this heap of merit;

dm: It does not bear comparison to a thousandth part, a hundred-thousandth part, a number, a measure, a calculation, an analogy, a likeness, or even a cause.
gm: nor a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part; nor does it admit of calculation, measure, counting, comparison, matching, or causal connection.

dm: Subhūti, if I were to describe the mass of merit of those noble sons or noble daughters who would fully uphold as much of this mass of merit as there is, sentient beings would become bewildered and their minds would be troubled.
gm: Subhūti, if I were to express the heap of merit of those sons of noble family or daughters of noble family, however great a heap of merit those sons of noble family or daughters of noble family will fully hold at that time, sentient beings would go mad and their minds would be confounded.

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, this Dharma discourse is inconceivable.
gm: Moreover, Subhūti, this dharma discourse is inconceivable,

dm: You should know that its ripening is also inconceivable.
gm: and its ripening should also be known to be simply inconceivable.

dm: Then, the venerable Subhūti addressed the Blessed One in this way:
gm: Then the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:

dm: Blessed One, how should those who have correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle abide?
gm: Blessed One, how should those who have correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle dwell?

dm: How should they practice?
gm: How should they practice?

dm: How should the mind be held?
gm: How should they fully control their minds?

dm: When he had spoken thus, the Blessed One addressed the venerable Subhūti in this way:
gm: When he had said this, the Blessed One said this to the venerable Subhūti:

dm: Subhūti, in this regard, one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think thus: "I shall lead all sentient beings to final nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder."
gm: Subhūti, here one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think thus: 'I will lead all sentient beings to complete nirvāṇa in the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder of the aggregates.

dm: Even though immeasurable sentient beings are led to final nirvāṇa in this way, one should generate the mind with the thought that not even one sentient being has been led to final nirvāṇa.
gm: Even though immeasurable sentient beings have been led to complete nirvāṇa in this way, no sentient being whatsoever has been led to complete nirvāṇa'—thus should they generate the mind.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, if a bodhisattva engages in the perception of a sentient being, they should not be called a bodhisattva;
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, if a bodhisattva engages in the perception of a sentient being, they are not to be called a bodhisattva,

dm: and if they engage in the perception of a person, they should not be called a bodhisattva.
gm: and even if they engage in a perception up to that of a person, it is because they are not to be called a bodhisattva.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, it is because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that can be called "having correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle."
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, it is because there is no dharma whatsoever called 'one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle'.

dm: Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: Subhūti, what do you think?

dm: Do you think that there is any phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has fully realized as unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment from the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara?
gm: Do you think there is any dharma whatsoever by which the Tathāgata fully awakened to unsurpassable, perfectly complete awakening from the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara?

dm: When he had spoken those words, the venerable Subhūti addressed the Blessed One as follows:
gm: When he had said this, the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:

dm: Blessed One, there is no phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has fully realized as unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment from the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara.
gm: Blessed One, there is no dharma whatsoever by which the Tathāgata fully awakened to unsurpassable, perfectly complete awakening from the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara.

dm: When he had spoken thus, the Blessed One addressed the venerable Subhūti in this way:
gm: When he had said this, the Blessed One said this to the venerable Subhūti:

dm: Subhūti, it is so. It is just so.
gm: Subhūti, it is so, it is so.

dm: There is no phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has fully realized as unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment from the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara.
gm: There is no dharma whatsoever by which the Tathāgata fully awakened to unsurpassable, perfectly complete awakening from the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara.

dm: Subhūti, if there were any phenomenon that the Tathāgata had fully realized as enlightenment, the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara would not have given me the prophecy, saying, "Young Brahmin, in a future time, you will become the Tathāgata, Arhat, Perfectly Complete Buddha named Śākyamuni."
gm: Subhūti, if there had been some dharma by which the Tathāgata fully awakened, the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara would not have prophesied to me, 'Brahmin boy, in a future time you will become a tathāgata, an arhat, a perfectly complete buddha named Śākyamuni.'

dm: Subhūti, because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has fully realized as unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment,
gm: Subhūti, since there is no dharma whatsoever by which the Tathāgata fully awakened to unsurpassable, perfectly complete awakening,

dm: for that reason, the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara prophesied to me, "Young Brahmin, in a future time, you will become the Tathāgata, Arhat, Perfectly Complete Buddha named Śākyamuni."
gm: therefore the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara prophesied to me, 'Brahmin boy, in a future time you will become a tathāgata, an arhat, a perfectly complete buddha named Śākyamuni.'

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, because the term "Tathāgata" is a designation for the true suchness.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, 'Tathāgata' is a designation for true suchness.

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if anyone were to say that the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha, has fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment, that person is speaking falsely.
gm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if anyone were to speak thus: 'The Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete buddha fully awakened to unsurpassable, perfectly complete awakening,' he would be speaking falsely.

dm: The Tathāgata speaks of them as "bodhisattvas," calling them "bodhisattvas."
gm: That one is called 'a bodhisattva, a bodhisattva' by the Tathāgata.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has fully awakened to as unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, it is because there is no dharma whatsoever by which the Tathāgata fully awakened to unsurpassable, perfectly complete awakening.

dm: Subhūti, regarding the phenomena that the Tathāgata has fully awakened to, or what he has taught, there is neither truth nor falsehood.
gm: Subhūti, in the dharma that the Tathāgata fully awakened to or taught, there is neither truth nor falsehood.

dm: Therefore, the Tathāgata has declared that all phenomena are the qualities of a Buddha.
gm: Therefore, the Tathāgata has taught that all dharmas are the Buddha's dharmas.

dm: Subhūti, what are called "all phenomena" are all non-phenomena.
gm: Subhūti, as for what is called 'all dharmas,' they are all non-dharmas.

dm: Therefore, all phenomena are called the qualities of a Buddha.
gm: Therefore, all dharmas are called the Buddha's dharmas.

dm: Subhūti, it is like this: for example, a person who possesses a human body and has become a great body.
gm: Subhūti, it is like, for example, a person endowed with a human body who has a large body.

dm: The venerable Subhūti replied, "Blessed One, that which the Tathāgata has spoken of as a person possessing a human body and a great body, the Tathāgata has spoken of as having no body."
gm: Venerable Subhūti said, "Blessed One, as for what the Tathāgata has taught as 'a person endowed with a human body and having a large body', the Tathāgata has taught that as being without a body.

dm: Therefore, it is called possessing a body and a great body.
gm: Therefore, it is called 'endowed with a body and having a large body'."

dm: The Blessed One replied, "Subhūti, it is so. It is just so.
gm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, so it is. So it is.

dm: If a bodhisattva were to say, 'I shall lead sentient beings to complete nirvana,' that one should not be called a bodhisattva.
gm: If any bodhisattva were to speak thus: 'I shall cause sentient beings to completely pass into nirvāṇa,' he would not be called a bodhisattva.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, do you think that there is any phenomenon called a bodhisattva?
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, do you think there is any dharma whatsoever called 'bodhisattva'?"

dm: Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One, it is not."
gm: Subhūti said, "Blessed One, that is not so."

dm: The Blessed One replied, "Subhūti, therefore the Tathāgata has said that all phenomena are without sentient beings, without life, and without persons."
gm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, therefore, the Tathāgata has taught that all dharmas are without a sentient being, without a soul, without a person."

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva were to say, "I shall accomplish the arrays of buddhafields," that should also be spoken of in that same way.
gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if any bodhisattva were to speak thus: 'I shall accomplish the arrays of the fields,' he too would be spoken of in the same way.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, the so-called "arrays of buddhafields, arrays of buddhafields"—the Tathāgata has said that they are not arrays.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, as for what is called 'arrays of the fields, arrays of the fields', the Tathāgata has taught them as being without array.

dm: Therefore, they are called "arrays of buddhafields."
gm: Therefore, they are called 'arrays of the fields'.

dm: Subhūti, any bodhisattva who is convinced that "phenomena are selfless, phenomena are selfless," is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva by the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha.
gm: Subhūti, as for any bodhisattva who resolutely believes thus: 'dharmas are without self, dharmas are without self,' the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Complete Buddha calls him a 'bodhisattva, a great being'.

dm: The Tathāgata’s Possession of the Five Extraordinary Eyes
gm: The Tathāgata Possessing the Five Extraordinary Eyes

dm: Subhūti, what do you think? Do you think that the Tathāgata possesses the fleshly eye?
gm: "Subhūti, what do you think? Does the Tathāgata possess the physical eye?"

dm: Subhūti replied, "It is so, Blessed One. The Tathāgata possesses the fleshly eye."
gm: Subhūti said, "Blessed One, it is so; the Tathāgata possesses the physical eye."

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?"
gm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?"

dm: Do you think that the Tathāgata possesses the divine eye?
gm: "Does the Tathāgata possess the divine eye?"

dm: Subhūti replied, "It is so, Blessed One. The Tathāgata possesses the divine eye."
gm: Subhūti said, "Blessed One, it is so; the Tathāgata possesses the divine eye."

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?"
gm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?"

dm: Do you think that the Tathāgata possesses the eye of wisdom?
gm: "Does the Tathāgata possess the eye of wisdom?"

dm: Subhūti replied, "It is so, Blessed One.
gm: Subhūti said, "Blessed One, it is so;"

dm: The Tathāgata possesses the eye of wisdom."
gm: "the Tathāgata possesses the eye of wisdom."

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?"

dm: Do you think that the Tathāgata possesses the Dharma eye?"
gm: "Does the Tathāgata possess the Dharma eye?"

dm: Subhūti replied, "It is so, Blessed One.
gm: Subhūti said, "Blessed One, it is so;"

dm: The Tathāgata possesses the Dharma eye."
gm: "the Tathāgata possesses the Dharma eye."

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?"

dm: Do you think that the Tathāgata possesses the Buddha eye?"
gm: "Does the Tathāgata possess the Buddha eye?"

dm: Subhūti replied, "It is so, Blessed One. It is so.
gm: Subhūti said, "Blessed One, it is so;"

dm: The Tathāgata possesses the Buddha eye."
gm: "the Tathāgata possesses the Buddha eye."

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?"

dm: If there were as many Ganges Rivers as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, and if there were as many world systems as there are grains of sand in all those rivers, would those world systems be numerous?
gm: "If there were just as many river Gaṅgās as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā, and if there were as many world realms as there are grains of sand in those, do you think those world realms would be many?"

dm: Subhūti replied, "It is so, Blessed One. It is so.
gm: Subhūti said, "Blessed One, it is so;"

dm: Those world systems would be numerous."
gm: "those world realms are many."

dm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, I fully know the streams of thought of all the sentient beings that exist in those world systems, with their various and diverse intentions.
gm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, I fully know the streams of mind of various dispositions of however many sentient beings there are in those world realms."

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, the so-called "stream of thought" is spoken of by the Tathāgata as being without a stream.
gm: "Why is that? Subhūti, as for what is called 'stream of mind, stream of mind', the Tathāgata has taught it to be no stream."

dm: Therefore, it is called a "stream of thought."
gm: "Therefore it is called 'stream of mind'."

dm: Why is that?
gm: Why is that?

dm: Mind and Mental Factors
gm: Mind and Mental Factors

dm: Subhūti, the past mind is also unapprehendable.
gm: Subhūti, the past mind cannot be apprehended.

dm: The future mind is also unapprehendable.
gm: The future mind cannot be apprehended.

dm: It is because the present mind is also unapprehendable.
gm: Because the present mind cannot be apprehended.

dm: Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: Subhūti, what do you think?

dm: If someone were to fill this trichiliocosm world system with the seven types of precious jewels and offer it as a gift, would that son or daughter of good family generate much merit on that basis?
gm: If someone were to completely fill this three-thousandfold great thousandfold world realm with the seven precious substances and give it as a gift, would that son of noble family or daughter of noble family produce much merit on that basis?

dm: Subhūti replied: "Blessed One, it would be much."
gm: Subhūti said, "Blessed One, it is much."

dm: Sugata, it would be much.
gm: "Sugata, it is much."

dm: The Blessed One replied, "Subhūti, it is so. It is just so.
gm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, it is so; it is so."

dm: That son or daughter of good family would generate a great heap of merit on that basis."
gm: That son of noble family or daughter of noble family would produce a great heap of merit on that basis.

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if a mass of merit were to become a mass of merit, the Tathāgata would not speak of it as a "mass of merit."
gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if a heap of merit were a heap of merit, the Tathāgata would not speak of 'a heap of merit, a heap of merit'.

dm: Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: Subhūti, what do you think?

dm: Do you think that the Tathāgata should be viewed by means of the perfection of his form body?
gm: Do you think the Tathāgata is to be seen by the perfect accomplishment of the form body?

dm: Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One, it is not."
gm: Subhūti said, "Blessed One, it is not so."

dm: The Tathāgata should not be viewed by means of the perfection of his form body.
gm: The Tathāgata is not to be seen by the perfect accomplishment of the form body.

dm: Why is that? Blessed One, it is because the perfection of the form body, as spoken of by the Tathāgata, is spoken of by the Tathāgata as the non-perfection of it.
gm: Why is that? Blessed One, it is because what is called the 'perfect accomplishment of the form body' has been spoken of by the Tathāgata as no perfect accomplishment.

dm: Therefore, it is called the perfection of the form body.
gm: Therefore it is called the 'perfect accomplishment of the form body'.

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?"

dm: Do you think that the Tathāgata should be viewed by means of the perfection of his marks?"
gm: Do you think the Tathāgata is to be seen by the perfection of marks?

dm: Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One, it is not so.
gm: Subhūti said, "Blessed One, it is not so."

dm: The Tathāgata should not be viewed by means of the perfection of his marks.
gm: The Tathāgata is not to be seen by the perfection of marks.

dm: Why is that? Because the perfection of marks that the Tathāgata has spoken of, the Tathāgata has spoken of as being the non-perfection of marks.
gm: Why is that? Because whatever perfection of marks has been spoken of by the Tathāgata, it has been spoken of by the Tathāgata as no perfection of marks.

dm: Therefore, it is called the perfection of marks.
gm: Therefore it is called the 'perfection of marks'.

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?"

dm: If you think that the Tathāgata considers, 'I have taught the Dharma,' Subhūti, do not view it in that way.
gm: If you think the Tathāgata thinks, 'I have taught the Dharma,' Subhūti, do not view it like that.

dm: It is because there is no phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has taught.
gm: Because there is no Dharma whatsoever that has been taught by the Tathāgata.

dm: Subhūti, if anyone were to say that the Tathāgata has taught a Dharma, that person would be speaking falsely and would be slandering me, because they have grasped at what is non-existent.
gm: Subhūti, if anyone says that the Tathāgata has taught the Dharma, Subhūti, they would slander me by grasping at what is non-existent and false.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, that which is called "teaching the Dharma" is such that there is no phenomenon whatsoever that can be apprehended as "teaching the Dharma" or "the Dharma that is taught."
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, as for what is called 'teaching the Dharma', there is no Dharma whatsoever that can be apprehended as 'teaching the Dharma'.

dm: Then, the venerable Subhūti addressed the Blessed One in this way:
gm: Then the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:

dm: Blessed One, in future times, will there be sentient beings who, upon hearing such an explanation of the Dharma as this, will give rise to true faith?
gm: "Blessed One, in the future, will there be any sentient beings who, having heard such a teaching of the Dharma, will come to truly believe it?"

dm: The Blessed One replied, "Subhūti, those are neither sentient beings nor are they non-sentient beings."
gm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, they are neither sentient beings, nor are they not sentient beings.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, it is because the Tathāgata has taught that those who are called sentient beings are not sentient beings.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, as for what are called 'sentient beings', it is because they have been spoken of by the Tathāgata as no sentient beings.

dm: Therefore, they are called sentient beings.
gm: Therefore they are called 'sentient beings'."

dm: Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: "Subhūti, what do you think?

dm: Do you think, Subhūti, that there is any dharma whatsoever by which the Tathāgata has fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
gm: Do you think there is any dharma whatsoever that the Tathāgata has fully awakened to as the unexcelled, perfectly complete awakening?"

dm: The venerable Subhūti replied, "Blessed One, there is no dharma whatsoever by which the Tathāgata has fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
gm: The venerable Subhūti said, "Blessed One, there is no dharma whatsoever that the Tathāgata has fully awakened to as the unexcelled, perfectly complete awakening."

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, it is so. It is just so."
gm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, so it is, so it is.

dm: For there is not the slightest dharma to be conceptually observed or to exist.
gm: In it, not even the slightest dharma is apprehended or exists;

dm: Therefore, it is called unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
gm: therefore it is called 'unexcelled, perfectly complete awakening.'

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, that dharma is equal;
gm: Furthermore, Subhūti, that dharma is equal;

dm: Since there is nothing whatsoever that is unequal or equal, it is called unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
gm: because there is nothing whatsoever unequal or equal in it, therefore it is called 'unexcelled, perfectly complete awakening'."

dm: That unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment is equal in being without a self, without a sentient being, without a life-force, and without a person;
gm: That unexcelled, perfectly complete awakening is equal in being without a self, without a sentient being, without a living soul, and without a person;

dm: it is perfectly and completely awakened through all wholesome dharmas.
gm: it is fully awakened to by means of all wholesome dharmas.

dm: Subhūti, as for what are called "wholesome dharmas," the Tathāgata has taught that they are devoid of the nature of dharmas;
gm: Subhūti, as for what are called 'wholesome dharmas', the Tathāgata has spoken of them as being exactly non-dharmas;

dm: therefore, they are called "wholesome dharmas."
gm: therefore they are called 'wholesome dharmas'.
