dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if any son or daughter of noble family were to gather a heap of the seven precious substances equal in size to as many Mount Merus, the kings of mountains, as there are in the trichiliocosm, and give them as a gift, and if another person were to take from this Perfection of Wisdom even just a four-line stanza and teach it to others, Subhūti, that former heap of merit would not approach even a hundredth part of the latter, nor would it bear comparison, even up to the point of calculation.
gm: Furthermore, Subhūti, compared to any son of noble family or daughter of noble family who, having collected heaps of the seven precious substances equal in amount to however many Sumerus, kings of mountains, there are in the three thousand grand thousand world systems, gives them as a gift, if someone were to take up even just a single four-line stanza from this perfection of wisdom and teach it to others, Subhūti, that former heap of merit does not approach even a hundredth part of this one, up to not even bearing comparison.

dm: Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: Subhūti, what do you think of this?

dm: If you think that the Tathāgata considers, "I have liberated sentient beings," Subhūti, do not view it in that way.
gm: If you think the Tathāgata intends, 'I shall liberate sentient beings,' Subhūti, it should not be seen like that.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, it is because there are no sentient beings whatsoever that have been liberated by the Tathāgata.
gm: Why is that? Because, Subhūti, there are no sentient beings whatsoever who are liberated by the Tathāgata.

dm: Subhūti, if the Tathāgata were to liberate any sentient being whatsoever, that would be the Tathāgata grasping at a self.
gm: Subhūti, if the Tathāgata were to have liberated any sentient beings whatsoever, that itself would be an apprehension of a self by the Tathāgata,

dm: It would be grasping at a sentient being, grasping at a life-force, and grasping at a person.
gm: an apprehension of a sentient being, an apprehension of a living soul, and an apprehension of a person.

dm: Subhūti, what is called "grasping at a self" has been declared by the Tathāgata to be "non-grasping," yet it is grasped by immature ordinary beings.
gm: Subhūti, as for what is called 'apprehension of a self', the Tathāgata has spoken of it as non-apprehension; yet it is apprehended by childish ordinary beings.

dm: Subhūti, as for what are called "immature ordinary beings," the Tathāgata has declared them to be non-beings.
gm: Subhūti, as for what are called 'childish ordinary beings', the Tathāgata has spoken of them as being exactly non-beings;

dm: Therefore, they are called "immature ordinary beings."
gm: therefore they are called 'childish ordinary beings'.

dm: Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: Subhūti, what do you think of this?

dm: Do you think that the Tathāgata should be seen by means of his perfect marks?
gm: Do you think that the Tathāgata is to be seen by the perfection of his marks?

dm: Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One, it is not so."
gm: Subhūti said, 'Blessed One, it is not so.'

dm: "The Tathāgata should not be seen by means of his perfect marks."
gm: The Tathāgata is not to be seen by the perfection of his marks.'

dm: The Blessed One replied, "Subhūti, it is so. It is just so.
gm: The Blessed One said, 'Subhūti, it is so. It is exactly so;

dm: The Tathāgata should not be seen by means of his perfect marks.
gm: the Tathāgata is not to be seen by the perfection of his marks.

dm: Subhūti, if the Tathāgata were to be seen by means of his perfect marks, then a wheel-turning monarch would also be a Tathāgata."
gm: Subhūti, if the Tathāgata were to be seen by the perfection of his marks, a wheel-turning king would also be a Tathāgata;

dm: Therefore, the Tathāgata should not be seen by means of his perfect marks.
gm: therefore, the Tathāgata is not to be seen by the perfection of his marks.'

dm: Then, the venerable Subhūti addressed the Blessed One in this way:
gm: Then the venerable Subhūti spoke thus to the Blessed One:

dm: "Blessed One, as I understand the meaning of what the Blessed One has said, the Tathāgata should not be seen by means of his perfect marks."
gm: 'Blessed One, as I understand the meaning of what the Blessed One has spoken, the Tathāgata is not to be seen by the perfection of his marks.'

dm: Then, at that time, the Blessed One spoke these verses:
gm: Then, at that time, the Blessed One spoke these verses:

dm: The Fruition of the Dharmakāya
gm: The Resultant Dharmakāya

dm: Those who see me as form, those who perceive me as sound, have entered upon a mistaken path;
gm: 'Those who see me by form, those who know me by sound, have set out on a wrong path;

dm: Those people do not see me.
gm: those people do not see me.

dm: The Buddhas are to be seen as the nature of reality.
gm: The Buddhas are to be seen as the nature of phenomena.

dm: The guides are the Dharmakāya; since the nature of reality is not an object to be known, it cannot be cognized.
gm: The guides are the body of Dharma. Since the nature of phenomena is not an object of knowledge, it cannot be cognized.'

dm: Subhūti, what do you think?
gm: 'Subhūti, what do you think?

dm: If you think that the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha, has fully awakened to perfect enlightenment by means of the perfection of marks, Subhūti, you should not view it in that way.
gm: If you think that the Tathāgata, the Arhat, became fully awakened to perfect and full awakening by the perfection of his marks, Subhūti, you should not see it like that.

dm: Subhūti, there is no Tathāgata, Arhat, perfectly complete Buddha who has fully awakened to perfect enlightenment by means of the perfection of marks.
gm: Subhūti, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, did not become fully awakened to perfect and full awakening by the perfection of his marks.

dm: Subhūti, if you think that those who have correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle hold the view that any phenomenon is destroyed or designated as cut off, Subhūti, you should not view it in that way.
gm: Subhūti, if you think that those who have genuinely set out in the Bodhisattva vehicle have destroyed some phenomenon or designated it as annihilated, Subhūti, it should not be seen like that.

dm: Those who have correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle do not hold that any phenomenon is destroyed or designated as cut off.
gm: Those who have genuinely set out in the Bodhisattva vehicle have not destroyed any phenomenon or designated it as annihilated.

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if a son or daughter of noble family were to fill as many world systems as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges with the seven types of precious jewels and give them as a gift, and if a bodhisattva were to gain patience in the realization that phenomena are without self and unborn, then that bodhisattva would generate a mass of merit far greater, immeasurable, and incalculable than that.
gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to fill as many world systems as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges with the seven precious things and give them as a gift, and if a Bodhisattva were to attain the patience that this Dharma-discourse is selfless and unproduced, he would produce from that basis a mass of merit vastly greater, incalculable and immeasurable.

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, a bodhisattva should not take hold of a mass of merit.
gm: Moreover, Subhūti, a Bodhisattva should not fully acquire a mass of merit.

dm: The venerable Subhūti asked, "Blessed One, should a bodhisattva not take hold of a mass of merit?"
gm: Venerable Subhūti asked, 'Blessed One, should a Bodhisattva not fully acquire a mass of merit?'

dm: The Blessed One replied, "Subhūti, one may indeed take hold of it, but one should not take hold of it wrongly.
gm: The Blessed One said, 'Subhūti, he does fully acquire it, but he does not acquire it erroneously;

dm: Therefore, it is called 'taking hold'."
gm: therefore it is called "fully acquiring".'

bo: ཡང་རབ་འབྱོར་གང་ལ་ལ་ཞིག་འདི་སྐད་དུ། དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་བཞུད་དམ་བྱོན་ཏམ། བཞེངས་སམ། བཞུགས་སམ། མནལ་བར་མཛད་དོ་ཞེས་ཟེར་ན། དེས་ངས་བཤད་པའི་དོན་མི་ཤེས་སོ། །
dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if anyone were to say that the Tathāgata comes or goes, stands, sits, or lies down, that person does not understand the meaning of what I have taught.
gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if anyone were to say that the Tathāgata goes, or comes, or stands, or sits, or lies down, he does not understand the meaning of what I have taught.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, the one called Tathāgata does not go anywhere, nor does he come from anywhere.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, the one called "the Tathāgata" has not gone anywhere and has not come from anywhere.

dm: Therefore, he is called the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Complete Buddha.
gm: Therefore he is called the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly and fully awakened Buddha.

dm: The Most Minute Particles
gm: Subtle Particles

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if a noble son or a noble daughter were to take all the earth-dust particles in the trichiliocosm world-system and reduce them to a collection of the finest atoms, what do you think, Subhūti? Would that collection of the finest atoms be numerous?
gm: Moreover, Subhūti, if any son of good family or daughter of good family were to grind as many particles of earth as there are in the trichiliocosm, the great thousandfold world system, into powder so that they become, for example, like a mass of fine atoms, what do you think, Subhūti, would that mass of fine atoms be large?

dm: Subhūti replied, "It is so, Bhagavan.
gm: Subhūti said, 'Blessed One, it is so;

dm: That collection of the finest atoms would be numerous."
gm: that mass of fine atoms would be large.

dm: Why is that? Bhagavan, if a collection of the finest atoms were to exist, the Bhagavan would not have spoken of a "collection of the finest atoms."
gm: Why is that? Blessed One, if a mass of fine atoms existed, the Blessed One would not have spoken of a "mass of fine atoms".

dm: Why is that? It is because what the Bhagavan has spoken of as a "collection of the finest atoms," the Tathāgata has spoken of as not being a collection.
gm: Why is that? Because what the Blessed One has spoken of as a "mass of fine atoms", the Tathāgata has taught as no mass;

dm: Therefore, it is called a "collection of the finest atoms."
gm: therefore it is called a "mass of fine atoms".

dm: What the Tathāgata has spoken of as a "three-thousandfold great thousand world system," the Tathāgata has spoken of as not being a world system.
gm: What the Tathāgata has spoken of as the "trichiliocosm, the great thousandfold world system", the Tathāgata has taught as no system;

dm: Therefore, it is called a "three-thousandfold great thousand world system."
gm: therefore it is called the "trichiliocosm, the great thousandfold world system".'

dm: Why is that? Bhagavan, if a world system were to exist, it would be grasping at a totality.
gm: Why is that? Blessed One, if a world system existed, that itself would be grasping at a solid mass.

dm: What the Tathāgata has spoken of as grasping at a totality, the Tathāgata has spoken of as not being a grasping, and for that reason it is so.
gm: Because what the Tathāgata has spoken of as 'grasping at a solid mass', the Tathāgata has taught as no grasping;

dm: Therefore, it is called "grasping at a totality."
gm: therefore it is called 'grasping at a solid mass'.

dm: The Blessed One replied, "Subhūti, grasping at a totality is merely a conventional designation."
gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, 'grasping at a solid mass' is itself merely a convention;

dm: That phenomenon is inexpressible, yet it is grasped by immature ordinary beings.
gm: that dharma is inexpressible, yet it is grasped by ordinary childish beings.

dm: Subhūti, if someone were to say, "The Tathāgata has spoken of a view of a self,"
gm: Subhūti, if anyone were to say: 'The Tathāgata has spoken of the view of a self,

dm: and were to say, "The Tathāgata has spoken of a view of a sentient being, a view of a life-force, and a view of a person," would that person be speaking correctly?
gm: the Tathāgata has spoken of the view of a sentient being, the view of a living soul, and the view of a person'—if they said that, would they be speaking truthfully?

dm: Subhūti replied, "No, Blessed One, it is not."
gm: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, they would not.

dm: "It is not so, Sugata."
gm: Sugata, they would not.

dm: "Why is that? Because, Blessed One, what the Tathāgata has spoken of as a view of a self, the Tathāgata has spoken of as a non-view; that is why it is called a view of a self."
gm: Why is that? Blessed One, what the Tathāgata has spoken of as the view of a self, the Tathāgata has spoken of as no view.

dm: Therefore, it is called a view of a self.
gm: Therefore it is called 'the view of a self'.

dm: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, in this regard, one who has correctly entered the path of the bodhisattva should know, see, and resolve to understand all phenomena in this way:
gm: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, thus should those who have truly entered the bodhisattva vehicle know, see, and be resolved upon all dharmas,

dm: "They should know how to abide without dwelling on the perception of phenomena."
gm: they should know them in such a way that they do not abide in the perception of a dharma.

dm: Why is that? Subhūti, the so-called "perception of phenomena" is spoken of by the Tathāgata as being without perception.
gm: Why is that? Subhūti, what is called 'perception of a dharma, perception of a dharma', the Tathāgata has spoken of as no perception.

dm: Therefore, it is called the perception of phenomena, the perception of phenomena.
gm: Therefore it is called 'perception of a dharma, perception of a dharma'.

dm: Furthermore, Subhūti, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva were to fill immeasurable and incalculable world systems with the seven types of precious substances and give them as a gift, compared to that, if a son or daughter of noble family were to take up, bear, read, master, or extensively and correctly teach to others even just a four-line verse from this perfection of wisdom, they would generate much greater, incalculable, and immeasurable merit.
gm: Furthermore, Subhūti, compared to a bodhisattva, a great being, who fills immeasurable and countless world systems with the seven precious things and gives them as a gift, if a son of noble family or daughter of noble family writes down, takes up, retains, reads, completely masters, or extensively and correctly explains to others even a four-line verse from this perfection of wisdom, they would produce infinitely and immeasurably more merit on that basis.

dm: How does one perfectly and thoroughly teach? It is by perfectly and thoroughly teaching in the same way that one does not perfectly and thoroughly teach.
gm: How does one correctly explain it? Just as one does not correctly explain it, in that way one correctly explains it;

dm: Therefore, it is called perfectly and thoroughly teaching.
gm: Therefore it is called 'correctly explaining'.

dm: Like a star, a visual fault, a lamp, A magical illusion, a dewdrop, a bubble, A dream, a flash of lightning, and a cloud— Thus should one view all conditioned phenomena.
gm: Like a star, a visual aberration, a lamp, an illusion, a dewdrop, a bubble, a dream, lightning, and a cloud—view all conditioned things thus.

dm: Concluding Sequence
gm: The Concluding Section

bo: བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ཀྱིས་དེ་སྐད་ཅེས་བཀའ་སྩལ་ནས། གནས་བརྟན་རབ་འབྱོར་དང༌། དགེ་སློང་དེ་དག་དང༌། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ་དག་དང༌། འཁོར་བཞི་པོ་དགེ་སློང་དང༌། དགེ་སློང་མ་དང༌། དགེ་བསྙེན་དང༌། དགེ་བསྙེན་མ་དང༌། ལྷ་དང༌། མི་དང་ལྷ་མ་ཡིན་དང༌། དྲི་ཟར་བཅས་པའི་འཇིག་རྟེན་ཡི་རངས་ཏེ།
dm: When the Bhagavān had spoken these words, the elder Subhūti, those monks, those bodhisattvas, and the fourfold assembly—monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen—along with the world of gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas, rejoiced,
gm: After the Bhagavan had spoken thus, the elder Subhūti, those monks, those bodhisattvas, and the fourfold assembly of monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, along with the world with its gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas, rejoiced and

dm: and highly praised what the Bhagavān had spoken.
gm: highly praised what the Bhagavan had spoken.

dm: The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra entitled "The Perfection of Wisdom that Cuts Like a Diamond" is concluded.
gm: The noble Mahāyāna sūtra called the Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā is complete.

dm: Namo bhagavate prajñāpāramitāye. Oṃ natadatita iliśi iliśi miliśi miliśi bhinayan bhinayan. Namo bhagavate pratyampate iriti iriti miriti miriti śuriti śuriti uśuri uśuri bhuyuye bhuyuye svāhā.
gm: namo bhagavate prajñāpāramitāye oṃ natadatita iliśi iliśi miliśi miliśi bhinayan bhinayan namo bhagavate pratyaṃprate iriti iriti mirati miriti śuriti śuriti uśuri uśuri bhuyuye bhuyuye svāhā

dm: Reciting this essence of the Diamond Cutter once is equivalent to reading the Diamond Cutter nineteen thousand times.
gm: By reciting this essence of the Vajracchedikā once, it becomes equal to having read the Vajracchedikā ninety million times.

dm: Ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetun teṣāṃ tathāgato hyavadat | teṣāñca yo nirodha evaṃvādī mahāśramaṇaye svāhā ||
gm: ye dharma hetuprabhava hetunteṣāntathāgato hyavadat, teṣāñca yo nirodha evaṃvādī mihāśramaṇaye svāhā
